messages.author: a6c78201f874807f
messages.subject: segfault in Knitr
parts:
I'm using Knitr within TeXShop.  It's been working wonderfully, and I've produced a couple hundred pages of course notes and solution sets with R examples.  Just this afternoon, the following code which had been working perfectly just stopped working.  Initially, I got a variety of errors and outputs, but the only error that happens repeatedly is the below segfault.  I pasted the error from the minimal version below my signature. 

I tried quitting TeXShop and starting again, and the main file started working again, and then it stopped working again.  Quitting and restarting this time doesn't help. 

Here is my .Rnw file, reduced to a minimal version.

 \documentclass [11pt]{article}
egin{document}
 
<<>>=
library(foreign)
NES=read.dta("nes5200_processed_voters_realideo.dta")
@

\end{document}

The file that I am using is 10 M and it is in the current directory, and it was downloaded from here:
http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/arm/examples/nes/

The example worked perfectly until today, and as far as I know nothing has changed.  Knitr still works well for everything else. 

Thanks for any help that you can give. 

Janet

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: segfault in Knitr
parts:
This issue seems more related to operating system capability than application capability. You did not explicitly mention your OS, but from the error message I am guessing it is a Mac. You can't "allocate" more memory to your application in Mac OSX, but you may be able to stop some other programs to free up memory.

When working near the limits of memory it can be difficult to get reproducible results. The fact that the problem went away after a reboot suggests that the OS memory management is showing bugs in this heavy usage scenario. I would not ordinarily consider processing 10M files to be strenuous, but that really depends on what processing you do with that file and what else you have been doing prior to the problem (straw that broke the camel's back).
